title_guess: Cost-push vs demand-pull inflation (Keynesian and Monetarist views)

segments.teaches: inflation means the general price level of goods and services rises over time

elements.what: grocery bag (goods) and delivery scooter (services) joined by '&'
price vs year axes with a rising line and a curved red arrow labelled inflation
small definition box pointing at the rising arrow

segments.notes: white canvas intro; the same intro composition is reused in E20

segments.teaches: price inflation has two causes, cost-push and demand-pull, tied to two schools of thought (pre and post 1970s)

elements.what: big ? above the heading
PRICE INFLATION heading on a pale panel
heading splits into cost-push and demand-pull branches
Keynesian school (pink) and Monetarist school (blue) pills with pre-1970s / post-1970s labels

segments.notes: canvas switches to cream background from here; school tags placed at left and right corners of the panel

segments.teaches: demand-pull: many buyers chase the same goods, sellers raise price from 50 to 65 and only some can pay

elements.what: Keynesian school + demand-pull inflation heading chips top-left
store with two product bottles below (supply side)
PRICE in the middle of a supply ---- demand line
person icons below demand with 'ready to pay 50 Rs' labels
row of blue person icons appears to show many buyers
price 50 struck, 65 written above
red crosses under most buyers who cannot pay 65
green up arrows on price and on demand
bottles move from store down to the few buyers who pay

segments.notes: running numeric example 50 -> 65; crowd grows from 2 to ~15; goods physically travel to the winning buyers

segments.teaches: demand > supply also happens when supply suddenly drops while demand is unchanged; price rises 50 to 60

elements.what: [DEMAND > SUPPLY] heading chip added after the demand-pull tag
store now shows only one bottle (supply fell)
price 50 struck -> 60; buyer's 'ready to pay 50' struck -> 60
'suddenly dropped' red chip under supply, 'not changed' yellow chip on demand
green up arrow beside new price

segments.notes: same layout reset to 2 buyers; second running example 50 -> 60

segments.teaches: supply-side shortfall inflation is called bottleneck (structural) inflation

elements.what: funnel/bottleneck of coloured dots narrowing into the store
pink band drawn over the store-price-demand area
BOTTLENECK INFLATION label
short explanation: supply hurdles, hazards or policy hurt supply
[STRUCTURAL INFLATION] chip under the text
explanation text gets a blue highlighter

segments.notes: naming a mechanism after showing it; synonym chip added below

segments.teaches: recap: demand-pull branch is done (demand > supply)

elements.what: PRICE INFLATION tree returns
green/purple tick on the demand-pull branch
[DEMAND > SUPPLY] note under the ticked branch

segments.notes: progress-map recap: returns to the earlier tree and ticks the finished branch before the next one

segments.teaches: cost-push: producer costs rise, price rises 50 to 55, buyers must pay more

elements.what: Keynesian school + cost-push inflation heading chips
factory with smoke -> arrow -> store with bottles
PRICE on the supply ---- demand line
yellow COST chip with 'increase' under it
price 50 struck -> 55; both buyers' 50 struck -> 55
green up arrows on cost and on price
thumbnail card of another channel video (inflation tax) showing a real politician's photo, bottom-left

segments.notes: same store/price/demand template as demand-pull, with a factory prepended; running example 50 -> 55; cross-promo thumbnail pops in at the end (do not reuse)

segments.teaches: Monetarists: both kinds need extra money with consumers; cost-push alone cannot last, so it is not an independent theory

elements.what: small PRICE INFLATION tree at top, both branches ticked, 'increase cost' and 'demand > supply' under them
pink band across both branch notes
large teal panel holding two explanation boxes (left: cost-push needs buyers; right: demand rises from extra purchasing power)
blue MONETARIST SCHOOL post-1970s bar along the bottom of the panel
blue elbow arrows looping from the monetarist bar up to both branch headings
dashed arrow from right box to left box (cost-push depends on demand)
conclusion line under the left box

segments.notes: two-school synthesis: Keynesian tree on top, Monetarist frame underneath wrapping both; key phrase highlighted in blue

elements.what: next video / playlist panels with app phone mock-up and store badges
